title: Principles of Quantum Superposition and Entanglement
text:
Quantum mechanics dictates that subatomic particles do not possess definite physical properties until they are measured. The principle of superposition describes this phenomenon, positing that a particle can exist in multiple states—such as spin up and spin down—simultaneously. Only the act of observation causes the wavefunction to collapse into a single, measurable state.

Furthermore, quantum entanglement represents one of the most counterintuitive aspects of physics. When two particles become entangled, they are linked in such a way that the measurement of one particle instantaneously influences the properties of the other, regardless of the physical distance separating them. This non-local correlation suggests a deeper interconnectedness within the fabric of reality.

These foundational concepts challenge classical understanding of locality and reality, forming the basis for emerging technologies like quantum computing and advanced cryptography.
